utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the witness can be released. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Just to reiterate what I raised earlier, namely that I hope that it is with the approval of the Chamber that on Monday I will complete the evidence of this witness and we will then start the cross-examination of Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And then after the end of Mr. Tihic, then you bring this witness back, or what is the problem? MR. DI FAZIO: There is an added problem with this. This witness is -- he's not a wealthy man, and he runs a small business in the federation, and now is the peak season for his business. His son is working in his business, and he's had to employ another man to take his place in the running of the business, and the witness is loath to immediately come back at this period of time. He says that later in the year or -- later in the year, there will be no problem in his coming back or very little problem in his coming back. But at the moment, it's a -- coming back straight away would -- in other words, next week, would cause him very considerable problems. I understand further that the Victims and Witnesses Unit have spoken to him and have something to convey to the Trial Chamber in -- connected with this issue. I don't know what, and I have not seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What you're leading to is that when you finish your examination-in-chief, you would like this witness released. MR. DI FAZIO: I'd like him released and to come back at some other time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Some other time for cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Perhaps that would give you more time to get hold of the documents which Mr. Zecevic is looking for before the cross-examination -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- of the witness, so if there is anything in those documents that the Defence would like to use for cross-examination, then they can have that opportunity. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Now, in terms of useful court time, I would -- I envisage, if the Chamber is minded to accommodate the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I will give the opportunity to the Defence to say what they want to say. MR. DI FAZIO: Then I would envisage this: Finish this gentleman on Monday morning, with his examination-in-chief, and he then leaves, goes back home, then call Tihic, Mr. Tihic, for his cross-examination, and that would take a number of days. As I mentioned to you, it's imperative that we deal with him next week. And then we could call another witness towards the end of the week, if Tihic finished early, so that the week would be usefully used up. And I understand that, although this is not finalised yet and I don't want to be tied down to this, but I understand Mr. Esad Dagovic would be called or might be called towards the end of the week. And then finalise -- and that way, the Court time would be usefully used up. I don't know what the Defence say about the matter, but that's the position of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to hear the Defence, whether there is any objection to, again, having this witness, when he finishes examination-in-chief, go away, come back later for cross-examination; in the meantime complete the cross-examination for Mr. Tihic and re-examination; and then perhaps hear another witness. Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could we have a second, Your Honours, just to make --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To consult, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we strongly object to this kind of conduct of the proceedings, for the following reasons: We understood that for whatever reasons, Mr. Tihic was an exception to the general rule that immediately after the examination-in-chief, we have the opportunity to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And we understood that for personal reasons, and Mr. Tihic being the president of the party and all of his functions which he is right now conducting, that it is appropriate that we agree to that, and, frankly, we didn't have any other alternative. But in this case, we simply do not understand what is the point of the Prosecution. If this witness is staying for Monday, then we can proceed, do the cross-examination of this witness, and then have Mr. Sulejman Tihic, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Even without the documents being brought forward?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the witness himself said that he can have it faxed by this afternoon, so I don't see any problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I doubt what exactly he meant by that, because it could be one document, it could be his own statement. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. It is my understanding, out of understanding the language directly, is that this document is actually either an indictment or some kind of a court decision, which is not the actual judgement but it's some kind of court decision, which will give us some, I don't know, understanding about the kind of the proceeding which was -- which he was involved in. But it's not that important at all that we will have to make another exception, and then at the very end, we might come into the situation as well that Mr. Dagovic, Esad comes, for example, Thursday afternoon, starts his direct, and then, because we are having a recess on that Friday, we are going to have then two witnesses who have not been cross-examined. And frankly, saying with all due respect, it is for us, completely unacceptable. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, the -- there are compelling reasons for doing that, for adopting that arrangement: Mr. Tihic's responsibilities. It's not just a question of Ramadan for him. I mentioned earlier today that he had acquired a new post or a new position and he is now president of the SDA in Bosnia, and his responsibilities have become -- have catapulted him into a different league, so to speak, and he is responsible for a number of more duties. And so from that point of view, it's extremely important that he be finished next week. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just to save the time, we are not objecting, because we have agreed before with our colleagues from the Prosecutor's Office that by the end of the examination-in-chief of the present witness, we will have Mr. Tihic coming over for cross-examination. That is what we have agreed with. But not that after Mr. Tihic comes, another witness, and we -- our understanding was that this witness, Mr. Ibrahim Salkic, will have examination-in-direct -- in-chief finished, then Mr. Sulejman Tihic will come for cross, and then after this is finished, we are having Mr. Salkic Ibrahim for cross, and that is how we end this -- the following week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So we don't have a problem, Your Honours, with Mr. Tihic coming over. What we have a problem is we have a third witness coming in between. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. di Fazio has understood that. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you did say that Mr. -- the witness we still have on the stand would come later in the year, which means he would probably be here -- because after our break, the week after next week, we will have three weeks' sitting, that is, up to the 7th of December, isn't it? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I don't know if the Defence can give us any idea -- and by that I mean, I should perhaps rephrase my words, can give us an accurate idea of how long they will be with Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Tihic? MR. DI FAZIO: No, Mr. Salkic. I don't know how long they will be. And if they were able to give us an accurate idea of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The time they will need for cross-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: -- the time they would require of him, then it might be possible to deal with him quickly and then call Tihic later in the week. But bearing in mind, bearing in mind, that Mr. Tihic must be finished at the end of next week. If we embark on that, then we are running a grave risk for the witness having -- saying to us, "Well, I've got to be back in Bosnia" and then chopping his cross-examination in two, and that's not desirable either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is our practice here at the Tribunal to also consider the witnesses' concerns. These are people who have undergone so many changes in their lives, and we have tried our level best to assist them to continue with their lives after giving evidence here, and we wouldn't like them to be detained unduly because otherwise the Prosecution will start having problems with future cases. The witnesses will simply refuse to come if that will mean disrupting their lives. We are quite sensitive to that. The point here is this: The Prosecution seems to say that they would rather have Mr. Tihic finished by the end of next week so that he can be finally released. If the cross-examination of the witness we have on the stand and the cross-examination of Mr. Tihic will be done within next week, that would be okay, if the Defence can indicate how long they think they will need, and then we can see whether or not we can have both cross-examination completed next week. MR. DI FAZIO: My initial reaction is: That would be ideal. May I just have a moment to confer with my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let me say this before you sit down. This particular case has got its own extra problems, because like this morning we lost half an hour, the other time we couldn't sit because the courtroom was required. So we have to bear in mind all these problems. I'm sure the Defence remembers also that. Because we can't even sit on a Saturday. I mean, in another jurisdiction, if there is a need, the court goes on on non-working days. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand, if Your Honours please. Now, could I just have a brief moment to confer with my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: But I must say, the ideal outcome for next week, from the Prosecution's point of view, would be this: Deal with Mr. Salkic, he can go back home, and then bring on Tihic and finish him by the end of the week, Friday, 5.00. Now, if we can do that, that would be an ideal outcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You consult -- yes. MR. DI FAZIO: May I just confer with my colleagues? Because I know that they have been speaking to the investigating officer. They may have more information that I've not acquired earlier this afternoon. But otherwise, I would regard that as the ideal outcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And have I to ask the interpreters to bear with us as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I just wanted to confirm that I've spoken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. di Fazio, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I just wanted to confirm that I've spoken to my colleagues, and I can confirm that would be, from the Prosecution's point of view, an ideal outcome for next week: Finish off this witness in his entirety and bring on Mr. Tihic for his cross-examination and then release him from the trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In order to accommodate the concerns of the Defence and also to stick to the procedure, the Trial Chamber is of the view that we shall have to sit longer hours next week, perhaps end our proceedings at 1830, in order to accommodate this problem. Because we are also sensitive to the other -- the witnesses' problems. So we will be sitting 1830.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I just -- I was anticipating something like that, and I was talking to my client, and apparently he said that he's up to his maximum at the moment with the sitting as we are sitting right now. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Sitting up to 1700 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The other way we can do it is because -- we can avoid bringing in a new witness concerning him after 1700 hours, so that he can be released, you will remain here. Because it's only to accommodate the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is entirely with the Prosecutor, and we have already talked in this respect with the -- concerning our talkings to the Registry about some other alternatives how we can deal with this problem. But it is entirely with the Prosecutor. We are fine with that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So perhaps for now we can leave it at that. We start on Monday, 0930 hours, hopefully, and then see how we go. So the decision is that we proceed with cross-examination of Mr. Salkic immediately after examination-in-chief, and let's see how far we shall go. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, but I understood that the point that the Prosecutor was trying to make is that Mr. Tihic is finished by the end of next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. With the addition of sitting hours, most likely we'll finish Mr. Tihic by Friday next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: One concern that obviously the cross-examination of Mr. Tihic, after having heard all the other evidence, may take long, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Bear with me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have to accommodate that way, by sitting long hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic. I'm sorry. Are you through with your consultations?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. di Fazio, you should be finished with your examination-in-chief by 11.00? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: You will be finished with your examination-in-chief by 11.00 on Monday? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I've just got the exchange to do and a bit of a wrap-up on property and his desires in respect of the exchange, and that's it. So they're not substantial matters. I've just about finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we believe that the situation is the following: We believe that we can finish the cross-examination of Mr. Tihic within two and a half days, which means that by Wednesday afternoon we are finished, and then another two days for Mr. Ibrahim Salkic, and that solves -- in our opinion, it solves the problem. Because we have already been told by the Prosecutor that Mr. Tihic is coming over, and his cross-examination is in preparation, actually, right now. And we understood that we are going to -- as I said in the very beginning, we understood that after the direct of Mr. Ibrahim Salkic, we are having Mr. Tihic for cross, and then, after the finishing of the cross of Mr. Tihic, we proceed with the cross of Mr. Ibrahim Salkic. Because all these other arrangements, like sitting longer hours and all that, with all due respect, I would have to consult with my client and see whether this would be possible, and these are the two witnesses that are actually concerning our case, our defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the Defence is saying that they prefer having Tihic first on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If he's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If he's -- well, I assume he's here or will be coming this weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the problem with cross-examining Salkic immediately after he's finished with examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we didn't have that problem until the Prosecutor said that it is essential that we finish Mr. Tihic next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But when did he say that? Today? Today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was -- it was -- we were notified, like, seven days before, and just today we talked about that. MR. DI FAZIO: It is essential that Mr. Tihic be finished next week. That's important to be -- it's important that that be done. However, now that the Defence have said that they can finish both witnesses next week, then there is no compelling reason not to follow the natural order of dealing with the witnesses, and that is: Mr. Salkic, I finish him on Monday, he's cross-examined, he goes, and then we start Mr. Tihic. Now, that is the normal way that, given the circumstances, that the matter would proceed. And now that the Defence have said, "Well, we can finish it in a week" and have given us that fair indication, then the ideal situation has been achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And there is another matter, of course, of Mr. Salkic. If we adopt what Mr. Zecevic was [sic] and switch, for whatever reason, switch the witnesses around, this man is going to be sitting around twiddling his thumbs, so to speak, losing money, and he's not a rich man. He's got a business to run, and he needs to get back to work and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. After consulting everybody and after announcing that we will sit longer hours, subject to what will happen to Mr. Milan Simic, like I indicated, we are going to sit on Monday from 0930 hours, complete Mr. Salkic, examination-in-chief, proceed with cross-examination, complete him, and then start cross-examination of Mr. Tihic. We have the weekend. The Defence counsel can prepare for the cross-examination for Mr. Salkic. They have already prepared for Mr. Tihic. I know that diligent Defence counsel would have done that already. And then whether we start him on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, even Friday, there should be no problem in terms of preparation for cross-examination. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 24 25
